transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-27
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Samir Gupta (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Nexa CTO), Liam O'Neil (Platform), Priya Rao (Security), Ethan Park (Data)

Summary:
Quick sync on onboarding progress and environment readiness for the Nexa Health POC. Covered: VPC/network access, initial benchmark plan, data access for eval set, security docs (SOC2, KMS), and next steps for a short performance run. Agreed on owners/dates.

Topics:
- VPC peering and creds
- Security & compliance questions
- Benchmark plan and success criteria
- Timeline for pilot runs

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, um we'll do a quick 30 minute sync and then Q&A, Samir you wanna drive the technical bits?
[00:12] Samir: yeah thanks Jordan, hey Maya, Liam, Priya good to see you. quick recap from last week - we got the model artifacts uploaded to the private bucket and confirmed quantized variant works with the runtime, there was a small thing with the KV cache alignment but we patched that.
[00:30] Maya: thanks, I saw that note in the deck. um our infra team still needs the VPC peering info — Liam is leading that but wanted to confirm what exact CIDR ranges you need and if there is any firewall / bastion requirement.
[00:45] Liam: right, also we need the exact IPs for the load balancer, we can't open everything.
[00:53] Samir: totally, for the pilot we'll need VPC peering from your VPC to our staging VPC, and a single bastion IP is fine. we'll share the redwood egress CIDR and the ALB IP ranges when we send the network diagram. should be the standard - no inbound 0.0.0.0.
[01:10] Priya: on the security side, can you confirm encryption at rest options, KMS support, and audit logs retention? also want to know if you have a customer-managed key (HSM) option.
[01:24] Jordan: yes, short answer is we support KMS integrations and you can either bring your own key or use our managed key for the pilot. we'll include SOC2 report and the audit log retention policy in the pack.
[01:36] Maya: perfect. also, do you have SSO/SAML for team access? we want RBAC to limit access to model routes.
[01:44] Samir: yes SAML SSO is supported, RBAC is configurable per-route; for the POC we can create scoped API keys and then switch to SSO once you're ready.
[01:55] Ethan: on data access — we plan to push sample records to the private bucket. do you need any schema mapping or any pre-processing?
[02:04] Samir: a little bit. if you can provide a representative sample of 200-500 records that mirror the production shape, that's ideal. we have a small ingestion script we can run; we'll share it.
[02:16] Jordan: ok next, benchmark plan. Samir?
[02:20] Samir: plan is a 2-hour window, run the standard throughput and latency suite: 1) 95th percentile latency at 1k token prompt, 2) concurrency ramp up to N threads (we proposed 50-concurrent initial), 3) cost per token estimate with batching and caching on. we'll need your typical prompt distributions; if not available we'll use the sample set.
[02:41] Liam: 50 concurrent sounds high, our main use case will be bursty. can you run a ramp that shows 5, 20, 50 concurrent so we can see degradation?
[02:52] Samir: yes we'll do stepped ramp. also we'll run the model variant with quantization and without to show cost/latency tradeoffs.
[03:03] Priya: for compliance, do you retain prompts? what's the retention policy and how are they deleted after the POC?
[03:11] Jordan: by default logs are ephemeral for the hosted run; for dedicated or private you control retention. we'll include the retention config options and an export script so you can rotate or purge logs.
[03:24] Maya: good. one more — is there any vendor lock or data residency issues? we need to keep data in US-east for this pilot.
[03:33] Samir: we can pin the region for the run; for Dedicated/Private you can fully control region. hosted may have multi-region fallbacks but we'll keep the pilot in us-east-1.
[03:44] Ethan: quick note on onboarding - when will Samir need access to the bucket?
[03:49] Samir: if you can grant a temp service account by EOD Monday that'd be great. we'll need read access to the sample bucket and a separate artifacts bucket we can write to for logs.
[03:59] Jordan: I'll follow up with the exact IAM permissions in the network/security pack.
[04:05] Maya: ok timeline wise we'd like the benchmark done by the week of April 6, that gives us time for compliance review.
[04:12] Jordan: sounds reasonable. we'll target the week of 2026-04-06 for the 2-hour benchmark.
[04:18] Liam: question — what's the rollback plan if latency spikes in production? we have SLA requirements for 99th p99 under 500ms for some routes.
[04:28] Samir: we support smart routing and can failover to a smaller/faster variant, or to a fallback hosted tier. for this POC we'll configure automatic fallback to a cached variant plus circuit-breaker thresholds. we'll show a config example in the runbook.
[04:44] Priya: will you share any perf dashboards live during the test? we want to watch token-level cost and per-route latency.
[04:52] Samir: yes we'll set up a Grafana view for the window and invite your team.
[04:58] Maya: ~okay great. any blockers from Redwood side?
[05:02] Jordan: none; main blockers are receiving VPC details and sample data from you, plus confirming the benchmark window.
[05:10] Maya: action items then — I'll have Liam and Ethan provision the VPC peering and sample data by Friday. Priya will review SOC2 docs.
[05:19] Jordan: perfect. we'll send the security pack and deployment checklist today. Samir will share benchmark script by Friday.
[05:26] Liam: one small nit — earlier you mentioned KV cache alignment issue, is that fixed in the runtime or a config flag?
[05:35] Samir: it's in the runtime but controlled by a config toggle, we pushed a patch to the staging image and validated locally. for the pilot we'll enable the aligned mode.
[05:45] Ethan: thanks. also please include estimated cost delta for quantized vs FP16 per 1k tokens so we can show to procurement.
[05:54] Jordan: sure, Samir will include a cost table.
[06:00] Samir: yep we'll run cost sims and include token-level breakdown.
[06:04] Jordan: ok let's recap next steps...
[06:07] (recap and owners)
[06:10] Jordan: recap - Jordan to send security pack + network diagram today; Samir to share benchmark script and cost sims by Friday; Nexa to provision VPC peering and provide sample data by Friday; schedule benchmark week of 2026-04-06.
[06:26] Maya: thanks everyone.
[06:28] Jordan: thanks, we'll follow up via email with links to docs and the calendar invite for the benchmark.
[06:35] (call ends)
